```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Set DUALCTL_RUN_VIGNETTE=false to build the vignette without running the
# (minutes-long) simulations.
run <- !identical(tolower(Sys.getenv("DUALCTL_RUN_VIGNETTE", "true")), "false")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = run, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, message = FALSE)
```

All numbers in this vignette come from a **synthetic plant** with
illustrative, unvalidated parameter values. They show how the methods behave
on the simulated problem, not what they would save on a real exchanger.

## 1. Scenario and models

A scenario is one YAML file. The quick variant extends the default fouling
scenario with fewer seeds, units and methods.

```{r load}
library(dualctl)
cfg <- load_scenario("fouling_quick.yaml")
fit <- load_model(cfg, variant = "fitted")   # what the estimator and controller believe
tru <- load_model(cfg, variant = "truth")    # the simulated plant (extra hardness state)
fit
tru$state_names
```

## 2. Identifiability: what do the weather and load teach on their own?

```{r ident}
ident <- identifiability_report(cfg, model = fit, seed = 1)
ident$classification
p <- plot_identifiability(ident)
p$p_bounds
p$p_spectrum
```

Parameters whose bound stays close to the prior under `disturbances` need
deliberate probing (velocity and dose changes) or the probe sensors.

## 3. One season: probe arm, production arm, advisor

```{r season}
season <- run_season(cfg, method = "dual_infompc", seed = 1, advisor = TRUE, keep_obs = TRUE)
table(season$arms)
plot_param_convergence(season$posterior, unit_idx = 0)
ps <- plot_season(season, state_col = "Rf", obs_col = "obs_Rf_probe")
ps$state
ps$u_v
plot_advisor_sequence(season$advisor$ranking)
head(season$advisor$sequence)
```

## 4. Which changes produced the savings?

```{r shapley}
adv_unit <- season$advisor$ranking$unit[1]
at <- season_attribution(season, unit_idx = adv_unit, cfg = cfg)
at$shapley
plot_shapley(at)
at$aumann
```

## 5. Monte Carlo over paired seeds

Each seed fixes the weather, the unit population, the initial states, the
observation noise and the arm assignment, so methods are compared on
identical plants.

```{r mc}
mc <- run_monte_carlo(cfg, parallel = FALSE)
met <- summarize_metrics(mc, cfg = cfg)
met$costs
met$comparisons
pr <- plot_regret(met$regret)
pr$p_time
pr$p_final
plot_coverage(met$coverage)
met$probe_value
```

With three seeds the intervals are wide; read `met$comparisons$verdict`
before drawing conclusions. The full study (50 seeds, all baselines and
ablations) is `Rscript run_demo.R` in the package source directory.

## 6. Ablation (sensor noise)

```{r ablation}
abl <- run_ablations(cfg, which = "sensor_noise", parallel = FALSE)
plot_ablations(abl)
```
